scenario: [LLOG.15.1] and [IRET.12.2]: a logical fact's last justification ends when its justifier's LHS no longer matches, "whatever ends the match" ([LLOG.15.1]), and a `withdraw` of the rule's own trigger is one such end. "The engine must retract exactly the logical facts [LLOG.2.5] leaves unsupported" ([IRET.12.2]), and when an activation ends because a supporting fact in the LHS was retracted, each logical fact it supports loses that justification and is retracted at zero. Rule `arm` matches the explicit `Trig t`, logs, emits `L logical v: t.v` and then withdraws `t` (an emit before the `withdraw` is legal, [LLOG.11.9]). The withdraw ends the very activation that is firing, so `L(1)`'s only justification ends with it, and `L(1)` is retracted in the same pump. Rule `live` joins `L` with a `Probe` asserted in a later pump and would log if `L(1)` had survived. Expected: "armed 1" and nothing else. A runtime whose firing activation takes the not-yet-fired branch, which withdraws no justification, keeps `L(1)`, and `live` logs "L 1 is live". PATH PINNED: libds's `ds_rete_terminal_left_retract` (rete/terminal.c) taking the TMS branch for `engine->firing_act`, and the Mercury runtime's `ds.engine.end_justifications`. The lockstep scenario 111_withdraw_own_trigger (fixture 143_withdraw_own_trigger) holds the two runtimes to each other with fact ids.
rules_ds:
schema Trig scope explicit:
    v: Int

schema Probe scope explicit:
    v: Int

schema L scope logical:
    v: Int key

rule arm:
    Trig t
->
    log info "armed {t.v}"
    emit L logical v: t.v
    withdraw t

rule live:
    L l
    Probe p where p.v == l.v
->
    log info "L {l.v} is live"
